body.statement:
For every admissible pair with \(2\leq n\leq5\), the exact sharp coordinate-degree frontier is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 n & D_k(n)\\ \hline
 2 & D_0(2)=1,\\
 3 & D_k(3)=1\quad(0\leq k\leq1),\\
 4 & D_k(4)=2\quad(0\leq k\leq3),\\
 5 & D_0(5)=2,\quad D_1(5)=3,\quad D_k(5)=4\quad(2\leq k\leq6).
\end{array}
\]
In each nontrivial lower-bound construction an original directed coefficient separates all generic conjugate branches.
body.proof_tex:
The admissible range is \(0\leq k\leq(n-1)(n-2)/2\). For \(n=2\), this forces \(k=0\), and \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) gives \(D_0(2)=1\).

For \(n=3\), one has \(k\in\{0,1\}\). The two-block conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:small\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maxima}\) gives \(d_e(G)\leq1\) for every finite query in either class. Since every triple with zero excess also belongs to every larger admissible budget class,
\[
 \mathcal G_{3,0}\subseteq\mathcal G_{3,k}.
\]
Together with the tree witness \(D_0(3)=1\) from \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\), this gives the reverse inequality. Hence \(D_k(3)=1\).

For \(n=4\), the three-block bound gives \(d_e(G)\leq2\) for every finite query and every admissible \(k\). The inclusion \(\mathcal G_{4,0}\subseteq\mathcal G_{4,k}\) and the separating degree-two tree witness in \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) give \(D_k(4)\geq2\). Thus \(D_k(4)=2\) for \(0\leq k\leq3\).

For \(n=5,k=0\), the tree result gives \(D_0(5)=2\). For \(k=1\), the special five-edge bound in \(\mathrm{lem:small\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maxima}\) gives \(D_1(5)\leq3\), while \(\mathrm{lem:five\mbox{-}node\mbox{-}cubic\mbox{-}coordinate\mbox{-}transfer}\) supplies a graph and an original edge of degree three. Hence \(D_1(5)=3\). Finally, for every admissible \(k\geq2\), the general four-block bound gives \(D_k(5)\leq4\), and \(\mathrm{lem:five\mbox{-}node\mbox{-}quartic\mbox{-}witness}\), together with \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\subseteq\mathcal G_{5,k}\), gives \(D_k(5)\geq4\). Thus \(D_k(5)=4\). The tree witnesses, the cubic transfer, and the quartic witness identify the separating original coefficients asserted in the theorem; in characteristic zero their finite minimal polynomials are separable.
body.justification: The exact table removes every vertex size through five from the unresolved frontier.
